context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
